title: Porter's Five Forces Scoring Rubric - Indian Quick Commerce
citation: Porter, M. E. (2008). The Five Competitive Forces That Shape Strategy. Harvard Business Review.
description: Deterministic quantitative metric-to-score mappings connecting real-world Indian quick commerce market data to 1-10 force hostility scores.

thresholds.label: Fragmented / Low Rivalry
thresholds.description: Many players with small shares, decentralized markets

thresholds.label: Moderate Oligopoly
thresholds.description: Differentiated niches, moderate price competition

thresholds.label: Tight Oligopoly
thresholds.description: Fierce customer poaching, promotional delivery fee battles

thresholds.label: Hyper-Rivalrous Concentrated Oligopoly
thresholds.description: Top 4 control >95%, direct dark-store radius overlap within 1.5 km

newEntrants.metricName: Dark Store Capex & Cash Burn Barrier
newEntrants.currentMetricValue: ₹35-45L per dark store capex + $15-20M/mo burn needed

thresholds.label: Negligible Capex (<₹10L/node)
thresholds.description: Low capital barrier, swift entrant proliferation

thresholds.label: Moderate Capex (₹10-25L/node)
thresholds.description: Regional entrants can enter with angel backing

thresholds.label: High Capex Moat (₹25-45L/node + dense dark store grid)
thresholds.description: High entry barrier, but deep-pocketed tech giants (Flipkart, Amazon) can enter

thresholds.label: Impenetrable Capital Moat (>₹50L/node + regulatory monopolies)
thresholds.description: Natural monopoly or extreme capital barrier

substitutes.metricName: Physical Proximity & Price Advantage of Kiranas & Supermarkets
substitutes.currentMetricValue: 12M+ Kiranas across India + D-Mart 10-15% cheaper bulk staples

thresholds.label: No Realistic Substitute
thresholds.description: Proprietary irreplaceable service with zero alternatives

thresholds.label: Weak Substitutes
thresholds.description: Alternatives are significantly slower (>2 days) or inconvenient

thresholds.label: Strong Substitutes (Kiranas & Scheduled E-com)
thresholds.description: Mom-and-pop Kiranas in 200m walking distance + next-day slots offer cheaper staples

thresholds.label: Dominant Substitutes
thresholds.description: Substitutes are cheaper, identical quality, and readily accessible

buyerPower.currentMetricValue: 68% urban multi-homing + order cancellation on ₹3 fee increase

thresholds.label: Captive Buyers
thresholds.description: Zero alternative platforms, high switching costs, mandatory lock-in

thresholds.label: Moderate Buyer Power
thresholds.description: Moderate multi-homing, mild loyalty program retention

thresholds.label: High Multi-Homing & High Elasticity
thresholds.description: 68% multi-home across Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart; zero switching cost

thresholds.label: Extreme Buyer Dominance
thresholds.description: Extreme price sensitivity; immediate churn on any price increase

supplierPower.metricName: Top FMCG Brand Concentration in Grocery Basket
supplierPower.currentMetricValue: Top 10 FMCG brands represent >40% of staple GMV

thresholds.label: Fragmented Suppliers
thresholds.description: Commoditized unbranded produce, hundreds of competing suppliers

thresholds.label: Moderate Supplier Leverage
thresholds.description: Balanced negotiations; platform sales velocity gives equal bargaining

thresholds.label: High Brand Equity (HUL, Amul, Nestle, ITC)
thresholds.description: Must-have consumer brands constrain margins to 18-22%, though quick commerce ad revenue offsets

thresholds.label: Monopolistic Supplier Cartel
thresholds.description: Exclusive IP suppliers dictating pricing and shelf terms
